\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{चोरी} (chorī)}{चोरी (chorī)}]{\mw{चोरी} (chorī) — a theft}

\label{lesson:MW-C243-chori}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for a potsherd, then the Marwadi for to sink.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{चोरी}}
\textbf{\mw{चोरी}} — \emph{chorī} — \textquotedblleft{}a theft\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{चोरी} \mw{माड़ी} \mw{बात} \mw{है।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{chorī māṛī bāt hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Stealing is a bad thing.
\end{quote}

A feminine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{चोरी}} (\emph{chorī}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{caurikā}, \textquotedblleft{}theft\textquotedblright{}; CDIAL lists Marwari \emph{corī} under it (CDIAL 4937).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chorī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chorī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{chorī māṛī bāt hai.} — Stealing is a bad thing.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marwadi for a potsherd, then the Marwadi for to sink, then say \emph{chorī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \mw{चोरी} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A theft\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{लूटणो} (lūṭṇo)}{लूटणो (lūṭṇo)}]{\mw{लूटणो} (lūṭṇo) — to rob; to plunder}

\label{lesson:MW-C243-lutno}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for to sink, then the Marwadi for a theft.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{लूटणो}}
\textbf{\mw{लूटणो}} — \emph{lūṭṇo} — \textquotedblleft{}to rob; to plunder\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{रात} \mw{मांय} \mw{कोई} \mw{गळी} \mw{मांय} \mw{लूटै} \mw{है।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{rāt mā̃y koī gaḷī mā̃y lūṭai hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Someone robs people in the lane at night.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \mw{म्हैं} \mw{पैसा} \mw{कोनी} \mw{लूट्या}, \emph{mhaĩ paisā konī lūṭyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{लूटणो}} (\emph{lūṭṇo}) is inherited from a reconstructed \emph{*luṭṭati}, \textquotedblleft{}plunders\textquotedblright{}; CDIAL lists Old Marwari \emph{lūṭaï}, \textquotedblleft{}plunders\textquotedblright{}, under it (CDIAL 11078).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happened.

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marwadi for to sink, then the Marwadi for a theft, then say \emph{lūṭṇo} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{खोसणो} (khosṇo)}{खोसणो (khosṇo)}]{\mw{खोसणो} (khosṇo) — to snatch away}

\label{lesson:MW-C243-khosno}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for a theft, then the Marwadi for to rob.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{खोसणो}}
\textbf{\mw{खोसणो}} — \emph{khosṇo} — \textquotedblleft{}to snatch away\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{म्हैं} \mw{थारी} \mw{कलम} \mw{कोनी} \mw{खोसी।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mhaĩ thārī kalam konī khosī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I did not snatch your pen.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \mw{म्हैं} \mw{टोपी} \mw{खोसी}, \emph{mhaĩ ṭopī khosī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{खोसणो}} (\emph{khosṇo}) is inherited from a reconstructed \emph{*skōṣati}, \textquotedblleft{}plucks out\textquotedblright{}. CDIAL gives no Marwari form in this entry; it lists Hindi \emph{khosnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to pluck out\textquotedblright{}. The Marwari sense, \textquotedblleft{}to snatch\textquotedblright{}, is probably a later turn of that meaning (CDIAL 13661).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khosṇo}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khosṇo}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mhaĩ thārī kalam konī khosī.} — I did not snatch your pen.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marwadi for a theft, then the Marwadi for to rob, then say \emph{khosṇo} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \mw{खोसणो} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To snatch away\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{गमणो} (gamṇo)}{गमणो (gamṇo)}]{\mw{गमणो} (gamṇo) — to go missing; to get lost}

\label{lesson:MW-C243-gamno}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for to rob, then the Marwadi for to snatch away.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{गमणो}}
\textbf{\mw{गमणो}} — \emph{gamṇo} — \textquotedblleft{}to go missing; to get lost\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{म्हारी} \mw{अंगूठी} \mw{गमी।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mhārī aṅgūṭhī gamī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My ring went missing.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \mw{वो} \mw{रुपियो} \mw{गम्यो}, \emph{vo rupiyo gamyo}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{गमणो}} (\emph{gamṇo}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{gamyate}, \textquotedblleft{}one goes\textquotedblright{}. CDIAL gives no Marwari form in this entry; it lists Hindi \emph{gamnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to be lost\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 4033). The taught \textbf{\mw{गमावणो}} (\emph{gamāvṇo}), \textquotedblleft{}to lose\textquotedblright{}, is its causative partner.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gamṇo}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{gamṇo}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mhārī aṅgūṭhī gamī.} — My ring went missing.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marwadi for to rob, then the Marwadi for to snatch away, then say \emph{gamṇo} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \mw{गमणो} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To go missing; to get lost\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\mw{ठगणो} (ṭhagṇo)}{ठगणो (ṭhagṇo)}]{\mw{ठगणो} (ṭhagṇo) — to cheat; to swindle}

\label{lesson:MW-C243-thagno}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marwadi for to snatch away, then the Marwadi for to go missing.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mw{ठगणो}}
\textbf{\mw{ठगणो}} — \emph{ṭhagṇo} — \textquotedblleft{}to cheat; to swindle\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\mw{वो} \mw{आदमी} \mw{घणो} \mw{ठगै} \mw{है।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{vo ādmī ghaṇo ṭhagai hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

Past (I …): \mw{म्हैं} \mw{गाहक} \mw{कोनी} \mw{ठग्या}, \emph{mhaĩ gāhak konī ṭhagyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mw{ठगणो}} (\emph{ṭhagṇo}) is inherited from a reconstructed \emph{*ṭhagg}, \textquotedblleft{}cheat\textquotedblright{}. CDIAL gives no Marwari form in this entry; it lists Hindi \emph{ṭhagnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to cheat, rob\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 5489).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happened.
